assumptions: Distances are straight-line distances in EPSG:3006 from each grid-cell polygon to the nearest extracted school point.
A cell is a gap only if the whole cell lies beyond the distance threshold from every extracted school.
The requested SCB age band is a proxy for school-age children; cells without a reported value cannot qualify.

grammar_note: Commands use a restricted command grammar: fixed English templates with explicit slots. It is not open-ended natural-language input; missing or out-of-range slots are asked back.
headline_template: {gap_cell_count} populated grid cells lie entirely farther than {distance_threshold_m} m from the nearest school and have at least {children_threshold} children aged {age_band_min} to {age_band_max}.

layers.label: SCB 1 km grid cells returned for the study rectangle

limitations: Population sums cover the SCB cells returned by the WFS BBOX filter (cells intersecting or touching the 20x20 km study rectangle, unclipped); they are not the exact population of that rectangle.
Distances above 2000 m are upper bounds: schools were extracted only up to 3 km beyond the study rectangle and edge cells extend up to 1 km beyond it.
Straight-line distance ignores the street network and is not a walking or transport measure.
OpenStreetMap completeness, school type and capacity are unknown; node and area features of one school are not merged.

plan_preview: step_1: load_population_dataset(population_grid_raw) -> population_grid. Standardise the raw SCB 1 km grid (M05 field mapping and value rules).
step_2: reproject_dataset(osm_poi) -> poi_3006. POI source CRS EPSG:4326 is recorded by the catalogue; project explicitly to EPSG:3006 for metric distances.
step_3: filter_attributes(poi_3006) -> schools. Keep OSM amenity=school points; an empty school layer is an error.
step_4: buffer_features(schools) -> school_service_areas. Straight-line buffer for the map only (not a walking area).
step_5: nearest_features(population_grid, schools) -> grid_nearest_school. Distance from each grid-cell polygon to its nearest school point.
step_6: filter_attributes(grid_nearest_school) -> coverage_gaps. Whole cell beyond the distance and enough children: a coverage gap.
report_templates: These cells hold {gap_children} of {total_children} reported children in the band, a share of {gap_children_share}.
The search used {school_count} school locations from OpenStreetMap inside the study rectangle plus a three-kilometre margin.

Population and child counts are sums over the {grid_cell_count} one-kilometre SCB cells returned for the study rectangle, including edge cells that intersect or touch its boundary, unclipped; they are not the exact population of the rectangle.
{band_not_reported_cells} cells have no reported value for the requested age band and cannot qualify.
